verdict.rationale: Gmail documents standard IMAP, POP and SMTP access with OAuth 2.0 and explicitly supports third-party clients such as Outlook, Apple Mail and Thunderbird, with messages and labels synced. The standards-based export half of the story is not documented first-party: the API's backup and migration use cases are developer building blocks, not an export feature. Community reports add caveats: IMAP IDLE does not propagate read-state changes, and Gmail's own export tools fail on 100GB+ inboxes. missing for 10: documented standards-based export (e.g. mbox) as a first-party feature, JMAP support, evidence that export works reliably for large mailboxes, full IMAP fidelity (IDLE flag changes).

support.subject: As a switcher, my mail stays reachable over open protocols and standard formats — IMAP/JMAP/SMTP access and standards-based export — so no client can lock me in

citations.quote: En el caso de los clientes que no son de Gmail, Gmail admite los protocolos estándar IMAP, POP y SMTP.
The Gmail IMAP, POP, and SMTP servers support authorization with the industry-standard OAuth 2.0 protocol.
You can add Gmail to other email clients, like Microsoft Outlook, Apple Mail, or Mozilla Thunderbird. When you add Gmail, your messages and labels are synced
